utterances.text: Yes, I can. On section B combat readiness situation, the last lines it is mentioned that Igman Infantry Brigade carried out sniper rifle shooting with 28 soldiers. After the practice in the sniper brigade, the shooting was assessed as good.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to just slow down.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Sorry. Those lines do indicate that there's organised sniper training as -- as is common practice for snipers.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And does it indicate anything to you about the -- the organisational form in which they are working?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm sorry. Whether -- are they -- how they're being deployed, whether they're working in a unit or some other function?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, I would say that they are working in a unit because they are -- the training has been done by their -- at brigade level. So that's -- that's not something in -- individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to the paragraph -- to page -- sorry. Page 2 of that document. If we could turn to: "The Situation in The Field."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's on the screen in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: It's on the screen -- I'm sorry. So it's actually paragraph 1. The first paragraph appearing on that page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes. If we could actually flip back to the page before in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, if you can take a look at the text under (a) where it says: "Enemy:", the text going onto the second page. If you can just review that. So those two paragraphs and then the beginning of the next page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Could I see the next page. Well, the only thing I would say that from this report -- from this report, it would seem that the -- the position of the report is quite accurate with details of -- I don't know if it's accurate but there's a lot of details in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And what is that -- what does that tell you in your experience about the -- about the control over the sniper units?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It calls for speculation and there is no foundational bases for any such knowledge of the command and control of snipers in this armed formation by this witness from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Perhaps I can rephrase the question, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Captain, are you familiar with how -- with how sniper and sniper units operate on -- in -- on confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: More or less over my own experience, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is there -- can you -- are you --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, I'll withdraw the question. I'm just going to tender this exhibit based on this -- 65 ter number based on the prior answers. One -- I'm tendering 65 ter number 15550.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 15550 becomes Exhibit P673, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P673 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I -- I do see that it's time for the break, and if Your Honours would allow me the indulgence I have maybe perhaps four or five more minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that we take these four or five minutes now and then take the break. You have until five minutes to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we turn to a moment back to a particular incident, which is incident scheduled F16, and that's the shooting of 14 year old Tarik Zunic, wounded on 6 March of 1995. And if we could have, please, 65 ter number 11213 on the monitor, and that is a UNMO daily sitrep for March 1995. And at page 3 of the document in both of the English and B/C/S, we see under point 8 subparagraph (a)3, it says: "Civilian male, aged 14 years, injured by," and there it says "SA RD in the left forearm at 061350 A," March 1995, "MAR 1995." And it gives a grid reference. And it says in the document there that the origin of fire was assessed at Sharpstone. And I'd like to go back to page 1 if we can for a moment and draw your attention to paragraph 3(b) which begins with: "During the activity in the area of Sharpstone," and goes on to say that "the Vogosca team received a telephone call from the CD R Radava BN," continues on that: "If the Egypt APC and his target practice area (Sedrenik) is not removed within 30 minutes it will be fired upon." Can you tell us, captain, what is -- what are the usual requirements for a chosen target practice area?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: If I had to work in a target practice area I would -- for small arms, I would use an area where I could visit the target I was shooting at, preferably a paper target to accurately know of -- write down my results and to be able to correct my sights.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you give us your comment based on your -- well, in your experience, have you -- do you choose target practice areas and actually practice your skills?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And given that, can you comment on that -- the -- on the portions of the paragraph -- the portions of the document that I've drawn your attention to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the -- the exact situation at the time, but I do believe that there's -- the target practice area where the shooting of -- the bullets ended up. It was separated from the origin of fire, so there was no way to check your results. So, for me, that would be an inaccurate target practice area.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And would a target -- would a usual target practice area be a civilian area, an area where civilians were living?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: For me, that would be not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours I would like to tender, please, this document, 65 ter 11213.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 11213 becomes Exhibit P674, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And my final question is --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In your report you discuss the training for target -- for -- at target identification, the training and the norms of target identification, and in your training and experience: If a sniper or a sharpshooter is not certain whether a target is a combatant or a non-combatant, what do -- what do the rules of engagement tell them to do?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Usually the rules of engagement would tell the shooter not to engage, but he could go higher up the chain of command to ask for permission.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, or -- the Chamber has considered the use of the chart. There's no problem with that, Mr. Groome. Did I understand well that it was mainly for authentication of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the Chamber would like to avoid that charts are used to circumvent our guidance in terms of associated exhibits. But if it's about authentication, then there's no problem. But the Chamber will, if at any later stage other charts are used, always clearly keep in mind its own guidance on number of associated exhibits and the importance of associated exhibits, but that apparently plays no role here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. These are purely medical records with respect to victims of some of the shelling and sniping victims incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And mainly that they are authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will have some questions today for you to try and clarify portions of your testimony and better understand your opinions and the bases for the same. First of all, I do want to stress and remind you that since we both are speaking the English language, it is critical that we observe a pause between question and answer to permit the court reporter and translators to do their jobs. Is that understood, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, likewise, I would ask to have you try and pay close attention to exactly what my questions are to try and ensure that the answers you provide are the most complete and most accurate answers possible to that question. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Then I would like to first spend some time going over your background. Could you tell the Court on how many other occasions have you testified as an expert in other legal proceedings, specifically on the topic of ballistics or forensic ballistics?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: They have all been for the ICTY. The first one has been in 2004, and it was -- some incidents concerning Mostar and the rest of the cases of the -- the testimonies have been related to Sarajevo, and I believe that they were on Mr. Dragomir Milosevic, Mr. Karadzic, and -- I'm not that good with the names, and on one other occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to those incidents apart from Mostar, would those be essentially most of the same incidents that are the subject matter of the report in this case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Most of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many times you have testified as an expert witness in legal proceedings on the topic of weapons and ammunition used either by the JNA, by the VRS, or the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: They would be the same as the ones listed above.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how many prior times you have testified as an expert on the topic of forensic criminology or crime-scene investigation in other legal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me apart from this report that you authored for the Prosecution in these proceedings, how many prior times have you testified in legal proceedings as an expert witness on the topic of performing analysis of probable locations of shooters based upon descriptions of incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No prior times.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to now take a look at your education and training. If we can first call up Exhibit P669. And that will be, I hope, your curriculum vitae, that you just looked at in direct. Thank you. And if we can first focus on the civilian education aspect. You list two institutions which you attended. And for the second one you identify that you graduated. Does that mean that you did not complete your studies and graduate from the TU Delft, because I do not see a similar notation for that institution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you confirm for us, sir, the Dr. Mollercollege in Waalwijk, is that a university or a secondary school?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It is a secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, sir, with regards to these two educational institutions, did you have any course work or obtain any degrees or certificats relating to the topic of mechanical engineering or any other type engineering?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I did not get any documents concerning those.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With relation to these two educational institutions, can you tell us if you completed any course work or obtained any degrees or certificates relating to the topics of ballistics or forensic ballistic analysis?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: As for forensic ballistic analysis, I did not get any, but for ballistics that is included in the sniper course and the fire-arms instructor course that did at the police academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With regard to the topic of ballistics or -- of ballistics, including but not limited to forensic ballistic analysis, did you offer any theses or papers on these fields?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect now to these two civilian institutions, did you ever have any course work or obtain any degrees or certificates from either in any scientific field which you believe assists you in the performance of the work you did in analysing the sniping incidents in the current case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Both degrees -- the secondary school that I visited -- that I attained, physics was in my exams, so physics does help with my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now if we can focus for a moment on the listing of the military courses that you have in the middle of the page of your CV, and if you could first clarify for us if any of the course work or studies that resulted in these diplomas and certificates involved a course of study in the engineering field or ballistics including but not limited to forensic ballistic analysis?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Several. The -- starting from the bottom up, because it's in chronological order, is [indiscernible] Sharpshooter course involves ballistics, the KCT sniper course involves ballistics, the KCT counter-terrorism course involves ballistics, the KCT fire-arms instructor as well as the sniper instructor course all involve ballistics and the teaching of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you again to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I apologise, I'm waiting for the transcript to catch up with us. With respect to these courses that you have now identified for us, could you tell me what type of instructors there were? Were these fellow soldiers, were they professors, were they officers, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would be a mix of those. So there would be fellow members of the military, one professor, and some officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to specifically these courses that you have now highlighted for us on these topics, how long did those courses last? Was it a matter of days, a matter of weeks?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Starting again from the bottom up: The sharpshooter course lasts for three weeks at that time; the sniper course at that time lasted four weeks; the KCT counterterrorism course, it lasts ten weeks; the firearms instructor course lasted four weeks; and the sniper instructor course lasted ten weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did any of the course work or training that you underwent in th military to obtain these identified degrees and certificates involve training in forensic criminal investigation or crime scene analysis of shooting incidents; that is to say, the activities that would normally be undertaken by police or military police organs?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the course of either your military career or your civilian career, did you have occasion to participate in or assist professionals in forensic criminal investigation of crime scenes where a shooting was involved, and, if so, in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you would slow down, equally that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise. I will endeavour to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so that we can be clear, am I correct that you have never had any type of medical training or education in the fields of forensic pathology or anthropology?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With regard to that study and training which you have had, particularly in the realm of sniper, sharpshooter, and fire-arms diplomas, would you agree that that was based upon the Dutch military protocols and standards and those of the NATO forces?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: They would be based upon but not -- but also include foreign weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when we're talking about these diplomas or certificates, they are all issued by Dutch military institutions; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Excluding the fire-arms instructor because that was issued by the Dutch police academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did any of your military training or course work, including that for which you obtained these diplomas and certificates, involve instruction about or study of the armed forces of Yugoslavia, the Yugoslav People's Army either in terms of their structure and organisation or their military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not in those courses. It did include -- it was -- there was some study involved for the deployments during UNPROFOR and IFOR in the mid-1990s.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's talk about the deployment with UNPROFOR. You say there was some study involved. Could you elaborate for us how extensive was that study in terms of, I guess, the time taken?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The study was limited to the Bosnia country -- country handbook that I was provided at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what kind of topics were included in the Bosnia country handbook that was provided to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I do not recall all the topics but -- as it was quite a long time ago, but I do remember that there was a list of weaponry used in the conflict by all sides listed in the -- in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you utilise that book in framing your opinions in drafting this report, in particular as to the armaments and ammunitions that would have been available to the parties?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I haven't listed it, so I didn't use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about now before your deployment as part of IFOR. Was there any additional instruction or training that you underwent at that time in relation to the specific circumstances of the Yugoslav People's Army, the Army of the Republika Srpska, or the armija of BiH?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There was some additional instruction but that would be mostly limited to intelligence updates.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that you are neither relying upon the instruction you received prior to your deployment as part of UNPROFOR, nor the instruction you received prior to your deployment as part of IFOR for purposes of the report that you generated for this proceeding?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct. I do rely on the experience that I had during those times.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did any of your military training or course work deal with the topic of the JNA tactics or training or deployment of snipers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, they -- not specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see that some of the diplomas and certificates are dated after the wars for succession in the former Yugoslavia. Did any of those courses touch upon the -- either the rules of engagement or target acquisition protocols utilised by the Army of the Republika Srpska or the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can focus for a moment on the Royal Military Academy and the Royal Military School that you have listed here on your CV as part of these diplomas or certificates, could you please confirm for me, sir, that you did not, in fact, complete the full course at these institutions that be would given for professional contract soldiers but, rather, you completed an abbreviated course?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is not correct. I did complete the whole course that was necessary at the time. For the military school at that time for my field it was five months, and for -- and as a professional, to become a professional officer, the Military Academy had six months. But it's still for the -- as a professional soldier, only the difference in course between long-term or short-term courses is more towards the -- the future. So I did complete them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. When you say that the only difference is between long-term and short-term courses is towards the future, could you please explain that? What precisely is the difference between the full course that they have for contract soldiers and the shorter-term course which you finished?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down for the sake of interpreters, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no difference between the course for contract soldiers and the short-term courses. All courses are now for professional soldiers. The difference is that if you do the full course at the military academy, you're more likely to end up at the General Staff level and for the -- for the military who do the short course, they will not get to the General Staff. Only after additional studies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to now examine your professional background and experience. Looking again at the CV, first of all, a general question: Did you have an occasion to perform services for or at the behest of any intelligence or counter-intelligence organ of either the Dutch military or some other NATO military or civilian body, especially when deployed in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the course of the various deployments with the Dutch military that you have listed, did you have occasion to experience or eye-witness live combat situations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before getting into specifics from your report and the prior testimony as to combat situations, in regards to those combat situations that you experienced or eye-witnessed personally, were you engaged at any time in the role of a sniper or anti-sniper capacity?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I was -- my function at the -- those days during UNPROFOR was as a sharpshooter. I did not -- I was not involved in the combat operations -- situations as sharpshooter. And for the IFOR deployment, I was a sniper but I was not the -- I was not functioning as a sniper in a -- the combat situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that during combat situations snipers or sniper teams often a faced with less than ideal circumstances and, thus, are required to operate outside of textbook experiences without the benefit of all the best equipment and best supplies that would be foreseen and taught in training for the performance of their duties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, that's five questions in one, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I guess it is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And apart from that is not very specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would -- perhaps I'd rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not very clear either. Less than ideal circumstances. I lived 90 per cent of my life in less than ideal circumstances. So if that is your criteria, could you please be concrete and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's -- let's limit it, sir, to combat situations. Would you agree with me that in combat situations there are occasions where personnel have to operate without all of the best equipment or best supplies that had been foreseen as part of their training.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I think that would be an accurate description of most of the combat situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, now, if I can tie that to part of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to 65 ter number 28451 and page 5 of the English in e-court, and page 8 in B/C/S, and these pages can be broadcast as they do not have any of the redacted information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ivetic. Is it 28451 or 28541?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Maybe it's 28541.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 28451 is P316, Your Honours. Document 28451 is P316, already admitted in October 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's 28541 that we need. I apologise. And again, it will be page 5 of the English; page 8 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, if you have the hard copy in front you it's obviously page 4 of 84 in the hard copy. And here you talk about the equipment of a sniper team. And now tying this together with the question that I just asked you and you just answered, have you experienced or have you heard of others in your field having experienced combat situations where they were forced to operate as a sniper without benefit of all the full inventory of equipment and/or personnel that you have listed here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes -- yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you therefore permit the possibility that either Army of Republika Srpska or Armija BiH snipers operating in Sarajevo during 1992 to 1995 may have experienced circumstances where they, too, did not have access to a full inventory of equipment, such as a spotting scope, binoculars, or even did not have a spotter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I would permit that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, for the record, this part of your report is limited to your knowledge of NATO armies and you are not suggesting any expertise on your part as to how a sniper in either the Armija of BiH or Army of Republika Srpska would be equipped as a matter of standard issue. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can clear up one more item from this section of your report. At page 4 in the English, and page 6 of the B/C/S, you outline tasks and deployment of the sniper and training of a sniper. And among these items, you include several times the necessity of a sniper team to consist of two persons. So, again, I want to make sure that this is in relation to your experience and knowledge as to NATO armies and that you are not suggesting any expertise or knowledge of such factors in relation to the Army of Republika Srpska or the Armija of BiH. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not completely. The knowledge is not limited to NATO armies. It does not include, as you say, the Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of BiH, but it does include other armies outside of NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you expect, sir, that such things would be regulated by other armies including by the Army of Republika Srpska or the Armija of BiH by manuals and regulations that would be promulgated and published?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you yourself studied or reviewed any manuals or regulations that were promulgated by either the Army of Republika Srpska of the Army of BiH as to the standard-issue equipment or standard structure of sniper teams?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you feel, therefore, that would you have to defer to other professionals in your field for these precise factors who have had access to or did study those publications, regulations and/or manuals?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I was just going to object to the formulation of that question, but I interrupted Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is unclear to the extent it is not obvious. If you haven't done something yourself, you should ask someone else who has done it, but that doesn't need -- unless you wanted to focus on which you have to defer as a duty. That is a different question. So the question is both unclear and -- but if you would rephrase it, Mr. Ivetic, so that we understand what you actually are asking, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For purposes of acting as a -- in an expert capacity providing testimony here today, sir, do you feel that would you have a duty to defer on questions of the issuance of equipment and the composition of sniper teams to other persons who have actually reviewed those publications, manuals, and/or regulations?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I maintain an objection to this question. The witness has been asked about what his -- what his knowledge is. I don't think it's for him to be asked whether he would defer to another expert in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, all depends on how much you would need that information for the expertise you're providing, it seems. So if you would be more precise and a bit more concrete, then we could proceed. But please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's try and be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you look at page 6 in the English and page 9 in the B/C/S of your report, sir, you have at the top -- near the middle of the page in the English, a section entitled: "Rules of Engagement." And here you refer to Appendix B of your report as well. Have you had occasion to become familiar with and are you holding yourself out as an expert on the rules of engagement that were effective and in existence in either the Army of Republika Srpska or the Armija BiH from 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I'm not claiming to be an expert on those rules of engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt the flow, but I saw the witness was struggling with the page numbers, so I would just like to note that the page numbers in the hard copy are behind by one for the e-court number in -- when -- when counsel cites the English e-court number, it's always one page behind in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I should have made that clear as I did earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can now turn to Appendix B of your report which in the e-court version should be page 93 of the English and page 135 of the B/C/S. In the hard copy, is the ERN 06699993, which is labelled as page 1 of 3. Now, sir, this appendix, if you have located it, is three pages long, and I have been unable to locate a single reference or citation to any authorities upon which you rely for the information that you have contained herein. With respect specifically to this appendix and these three pages of your report, can you identify for us any and all source materials and/or references which you either consulted when drafting this appendix or relied upon in reaching the conclusions contained therein?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I admit a lot of it is based on experience, but on the matter of camouflage and observation, that would be out of any handbook for sniping. Or camouflage in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic [sic], just for the record, the page refreshes you gave for the B/C/S should be 119 instead of 135. If I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it's only a 122-page document in e-court in B/C/S. And the part of the identification of targets starts at page 119 and continues 120 and 121.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the confusion. These long reports always seem to have issues with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no issue with the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With me counting the pages is the issue, Your Honours. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to this appendix on target identification, in particular, the section where you talk about the keeping of log-books, the taught techniques of identification, would I be correct in stating that this, too, is based on your knowledge and experience of NATO forces and is not meant by you to be held out as an expertise relating to these same topics within the doctrine of the Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It is based on my knowledge and experience of long-range shooting in general, not only NATO forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could you answer the second part of that question whether it is intended to be held out as an expertise relating to those same topics, i.e., the keeping of log-books and taught techniques of identification as it pertains to the Army of Republika Srpska and the Armija BiH?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would split that question in two. The keeping of log-books would very much surprise me if it wasn't used, since for long-range shooting, without the keeping of log-books, you'd be a very poor shooter. The taught techniques of identification is not something that is regularly in a course. Everything is based on camouflage and on observation and it is not -- the identification is not something that is taught. It is something that is -- comes out of experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If we can now return to Exhibit P669. And while we wait for that, sir, I'll again be asking you about your experiences in the former Yugoslavia. If I read your CV correctly, you have listed a deployment to Bosnia under the auspices of the IFOR from August to December of 1996 on the first page of your CV. And then, on page 2, you also have a deployment to Bosnia under the auspices of UNPROFOR from January 1995 to June 1995. Could you tell me if either of these deployments included any significant time in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There was no significant time other than passing through Sarajevo in the first deployment. The second deployment I didn't visit Sarajevo at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that the bulk of your deployment in Bosnia as parts of UNPROFOR was as part of the DutchBat in the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is incorrect. My company was based in Simin Han, east of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I misread the question. You only passed through the enclave of Srebrenica and spent two days there; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct. On a convoy escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As for the actual factual situation in Sarajevo from 1992 to 1995, that is the time-period of your report, do you feel that you would have to defer as to -- to someone who was actually on the ground in Sarajevo as to the position of forces, the position of the confrontation line, and the combat and sniper activity ongoing at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Again, I object to -- to these -- the formulation of all this as a deference to somebody else. I think counsel can just ask whether he has knowledge of those particular subject matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, that would bring us quicker to useful answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you, in fact, have knowledge as to the position of forces and the position of the confrontation line in Sarajevo from the time-period of 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What is that knowledge based upon?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The knowledge is based upon my visit to Sarajevo where I passed through several check-points, and it's based on remnants of the war still visible in Sarajevo during the visits that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you feel that passing through several check-points gave you a full picture of the position of forces or just with respect to those check-points?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That would be just around those check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- well, again, I would ask you: Do you think that you would have to defer to persons who were on the ground as to the position of forces and the type of combat activity that was ongoing at the time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have deferred to persons for the situation as for witness statements and other information, maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, have you ever -- strike that. I've already asked that. If we can turn back to your report. So that's number 28541. And hopefully my pages are right. I'm looking for page 84 of the same in English, which should be page 83 in the hard copy, and it should be page 106 of the B/C/S. Here, sir, we have a selection from your report entitled "Ballistics and Shooting," and this is approximately a page and a half in length in the English. With respect specifically to this portion of the report, did you have this part of your report peer reviewed by any colleagues in the field of your expertise?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to consult with anyone trained professionally in the field of ballistics or forensic ballistics analysis to assist you in preparing this part of the report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, why always remain on the abstract level? If there's anything wrong with this part, attack it directly because it's wrong with or without peer review. If there's anything. Because otherwise we spend ages on theoretical matters rather than on whether this is reliable information for the Chamber. Again, peer review is not a guarantee. If there's anything wrong, point at it. I mean, if the gravity is not existing in your view, let's attack the gravity part or wind drift or is it the details that for this bullet it would be different. Then by attacking that, we'll know what the quality of his expertise is rather than to know whether it was ever peer reviewed, yes or no. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. But we also have to again address whether the methodology applied this person with regard to this report is appropriate for the standards in the industry, Your Honours, and that -- you left that decision open and deferred for it in the decision on the 92 bis submissions, so I have to go through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is best done by pointing at where things are wrong in the report as a result of wrong methodology. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to this part of the report, can you please identify for us the source materials and/or references upon which you rely or which you consulted in drafting this section of the report.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The source materials would be the -- the several manuals that we have for sniping or for fire-arms instruction and just general knowledge on shooting in -- that's available to the general public.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could we first address the several manuals that we have for sniping and for fire-arms instruction. Which manuals in particular are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The base of my knowledge would be, of course, the Dutch army sniper manual. I do have to mention that most of the -- that about 50 per cent of knowledge is transferred verbally during courses, that not everything is written down in manuals. So a lot of it, a lot of information that I have gathered for the report is done by studying more sources or through the Internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect first to this Dutch army sniper manual, could you tell us its publication date and if a copy was provided to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It was not. There is no Dutch army sniper manual since it's Dutch army by itself does not have any snipers. It is within our special forces unit there is a sniper manual.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please provide us with a publication date for that manual so that we may do our diligence to review that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I could not. I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where that manual could be obtained?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That would have to go to through the Dutch Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In so as far as you stated that you relied upon it, do you have a copy of the same?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have a copy at my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have a problem locating and providing those to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I think so. I would have to go through my superiors and ask permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are there any other manuals -- I may have cut you off. Any other manuals or publications that you rely upon as source materials or references for the material that you have set forth in this selection relating to ballistics and shooting?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The publications are widely available on the Internet, so I would have to go on the Internet to get a list of all the sources. For manuals, the other source material that I have used - because most of it, the information is inside my head instead of straight out of a book - is in course material for the fire-arms instructor, the ballistics part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that course material different from the -- from the manual that we discussed from the Dutch special forces?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The material is different, since it's -- it's not a course for snipers, it's a course for fire-arms instructors and it includes general ballistics, and it's taught by the police academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would that be a manual that you have in your possession that you would be able to give to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Again, I would have to get a request to the police academy, if they have objections to -- to hand it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You start off this section of your report with the assertion that there are really no such thing as stray bullets. With respect to this specific assertion, is it something which other textbooks or reference books that you are aware of have stated or supported?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Would you allow me to explain myself for the sentence? A lot of the report is based -- I could go in very specific details about technical stuff on the subject matter, but I thought it would be -- would it be wiser to -- to try to explain the subject matter to people with less experience in that field. And stray bullets, like the word "sniper," are things that are known to a lot of people but everybody has a different feel for it. So that's why I included the line "there are no stray bullets" because a bullet doesn't travel on its own or just -- a bullet follows a path.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you mean to say that bullets are always subject to the laws of physics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They certainly are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the middle of page 83 of 84 in the hard copy, which is page 84 in e-court, and it should be the page -- in B/C/S that is on the screen. You say: "The above is just to show that for a long-range shot a shooter must either be well trained or very experienced to make first-round hits." Would you agree with me that shorter-range shots are much easier to accomplish first-round hits with?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you can follow my hypothetical now, if you have a situation where there are two or more potential sources or possible sources for fire that has resulted in damage or injury, would you agree that statically the more probable source of fire, if a single-shot scenario, would be the location nearer to the victim or target rather than the longer-range shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I don't believe that could be put in a statistic because it depends on the person behind the weapon and the weapon and ammunition combined. If I would put the same person with the same weapon, the same ammunition, at several ranges and have him fire from there, then a shorter range would provide better results.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's approach it this way, sir, theoretically speaking. Where you have multiple potential locations of a shooter when you are investigating an incident, or analysing an incident, I should say, and you have one that is a long-range target, a long-range shot, and one that is a shorter range shot, do you believe that it would be prudent and within the expected expertise of your field to ignore the shorter range shot and to focus only on the longer range shot as the potential source of the incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I could answer that question. It's always not wise to ignore possibilities when you investigate something. That's a general answer to this. And I think the witness could not give any other answer. But what you want to say is: Wouldn't it be wise to focus first on the short range, isn't it? That's what you are seeking to establish, that that would be the best way to?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think both should be reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I -- we agree on that at least. I don't know about my colleagues, but we agree that it's best to explore all possibilities and certainly not to ignore the short range. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page of your report in the English, it is also on the next page in the B/C/S, I believe, you give us here an example of moving targets and the speed of the 7.62 mm by 51 mm NATO bullet. Am I correct that you do not have sufficient knowledge and experience to quote with us with certainty as an expert the speed of all standard non-NATO munitions that would have potentially been in use in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I don't think you are correct. I have the sufficient knowledge. And given a few minutes, I would find on the Internet, because there are excellent tables and calculations for all ammunitions, barrel length and all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you then perhaps identify for me what manuals or references have you had at your disposal or reviewed to determine or verify the speeds of various types of ordnance, whether NATO or other?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Some of it is general knowledge in -- in my experience, but otherwise I would have to go to the Internet and get some of the web sites that I might use.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what some of the web sites are? Are we talking about Wikipedia, are we talking about Google? I mean, are we talking about specific specialised web sites or the general Internet, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's a -- for specific web sites. But, again, I could not give you the web sites now. I would have to go on the Internet and locate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's return to the long-range shot again, the type that you discussed on the prior page. Would you agree with me that, due to all the factors that you list on this prior page --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, page 84 in e-court on the English, page 100 and -- well, the prior page in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to all the factors that you list, is it more likely for a long-range shot to miss its intended target on a first round?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Compared to a short range shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And practically speaking, such missed shots would still hit up -- hitting something or someone; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: If that -- that something or someone would be in the vicinity, then that might happen, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if they miss and continue on a trajectory affected by these ballistics elements you have listed, they could potentially hit unintended targets, including, civilians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That -- that is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that you cannot exclude with a reasonable degree of certainty the possibility of a long-range shot missing its intended target and ricochetting off a hard object and taking a new trajectory, can you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would like to say that ricochetting is not something that would alter the path of the bullet. At a 90 degree angle, it would be just slight deviation of the path, but it would be a new trajectory since the speed will have slowed down and the bullet would have given -- taken a new shape, so there would be a new trajectory, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the report the ricochet effect would apply to both shorter range and longer range shots; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The ricochet effect is, of course, affected by the type of material that is hit, the speed of the bullet, the weight of the bullet, and a lot of other factors. But it's possible. It's applicable to any bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm looking at the clock. We are about to have a break. Most of the last questions I would say are all common sense, isn't it? If a bullet doesn't hit its target, hits something else, which it inevitably will do - I've never seen a bullet flying around for the next century - then of course that changes the path and the energy and -- I mean, do we really need this to be further explored? It should --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In light of this report I think we do because this report acts as if there's only one possible explanation for all this and since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then go to the findings of the report and challenge those on the basis. Ask for F1 or F10 or whatever, is there a possibility that it was a ricochet, and then, of course, we'll all understand what that means. That it's a bullet fired somewhere else, hitting not its target, or hitting its target and continuing its trajectory in a different way with different energy. Therefore, focus on the concrete matters rather than on the theoretical side of it, and refer to the three to the extent it becomes apparent that it has affected the findings. We take a break, and we resume at a quarter to 2.00. Witness first to be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you explain for us so we understand your use of the term, what range of distance between target and shooter would you understand and consider to be a "long-range shot" as you've used in your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Long-range, in my opinion, would be over 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to turn to another portion of your report dealing with the Unscheduled Incidents. It starts at page 69 in e-court which would be page 68 of the hard copy, with the text actually beginning on page 69 of the hard copy, and page 88 and onwards in the B/C/S. And, first of all, before we get to the specifics of these incidents, we have been provided a supplemental information sheet from your proofing session with the Prosecution wherein at number 11 it states: "The witness states that, to the best of his recollection, he was only provided the incident description, not the underlying written documents for the Unscheduled Incidents which he first evaluated in the Dragomir Milosevic case." First of all, sir, can you confirm whether, in fact, this representation by the Prosecution is accurate and truthful?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It is accurate but not complete. I was not provided more than the incident description for writing this report. However, for the previous report in which the incidents also were mentioned, there I did have another of the -- extra documents, only I've handed them back to the OTP at that time, and I haven't been able to find them -- to locate them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just so that we are clear, we are right now talking about the Unscheduled Incidents, the three incidents that are on the screen on your report. Is that -- is your answer also relating to those three incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, for the Unscheduled Incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. And now the findings that you have for these Unscheduled Incidents that are contained in this report for this trial, are you now telling me that that is based on something more than just the incident descriptions, that is to say that you had other material when drafting this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that other material is the material that you cannot find. Can you at least identify for us what that material would be?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I do refer in the first one for Nedzarici in the additional information, there I do recall that there was a witness statement by the two friends of the victim. But for -- since the initial document was written in 2009 -- no, 2006, the end of 2006, I -- I wouldn't -- I couldn't exactly state which documents I -- I had at my disposal at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the Prosecution kept any list of documents that it provided for you or which you stated that you relied upon for purposes of these three incidents, these three Unscheduled Incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the written descriptions or summaries that are mentioned, did you ever ask the Prosecution what the sources were for this information that was contained in these summaries or descriptions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Since I don't remember exactly what the documents were, I could not -- I could not form a question [sic]. I do remember that when visiting the locations, I was provided with information by the investigator with -- and the information that he had was from witness statements and other documents. So I did have the information from the investigator, but as for the documents, I don't know where that information came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me see if I can understand you correctly. First of all, when you went out into the field to examine these locations, am I correct that the investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor is the one that told you where the purported shooter came from, where -- the direction from which the shots came from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, he was amongst one of the sources that -- that told me of -- that gave information about the direction of the -- of the location of the shooter, but in the -- in the -- I think it is list of -- the indictment list with -- which states -- or the initial list that I got was an incident number, a date, a brief description, in most of the cases also mentioned the point of origin for the shooter, and a GPS co-ordinate. So it was not something that I had heard for the first time but it was something that was, again, pointed out to me by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This brief description which had a point of origin for the shooter and also had a GPS co-ordinate, is that -- is that the documentation that you no longer have, or is that something that you do still have access to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I -- I still -- I also don't have that documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, to be clear, when you say that documentation had the point of origin for the shooter and the GPS co-ordinates, are those point of origins -- point of origin and GPS co-ordinates that you determined or that were given to you by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, this was -- the point of origin in the documentation, it had the point of origin according to witnesses, from witness statements and the GPS co-ordinates as given, they came from the same source, so from the -- the investigator. And if the point of origin would coincide with my findings, then I would use the same co-ordinates and that point of origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And were there instances where the co-ordinates that were given to you by the OTP Prosecutor -- investigators did not correlate with that which you have found? I mean, how do we know that? Where is that reflected in your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would refer to case F12, which is the incident that was discussed earlier this -- this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, we're focussing now on the Unscheduled Incidents.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Oh, the unscheduled.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Just a moment. No, for the Unscheduled Incidents, I didn't change the GPS co-ordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, did you verify them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I verified them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the first of these Unscheduled Incidents - that would be at page 73 in the English in e-court, page 72 in the hard copy before us - you talk about the witness having civilian clothing. For the second incident - unscheduled, at page 78 in e-court, page 77 in the hard copy - you also focus on the victim wearing civilian clothing. And, lastly, at page 83 in e-court, 82 in the hard copy, of the English, for the third incident, and the position -- the third incident, you mention that the victim was not wearing a uniform? The question I want to ask you is as follows: Did this information -- did the information that the Office of the Prosecutor gave to you, which I understand that you no longer have and can no longer identify for us, did it include any information or descriptions from other witnesses as to the extent that combatants in Sarajevo during the relevant time-period were dressed in civilian or military clothing? The extent to which combatants would have been dressed in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No. It was solely the information for the -- for the victims themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any independent information or undertake any independent investigation to determine the prevalence of combatants wearing civilian clothing in Sarajevo during this time-period?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, I clearly remember from items on the -- on the daily news at that time that there was a mix, at least, of military and civilian clothing. On both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please assist me. This -- does this witness give any specific opinion about the status of the victim? Or does he just say civilian clothing, therefore, you could think of that person to be a civilian. Does he make any determination on the basis of his expertise? Because, otherwise, it's -- it's useless to ask him about this. He receives information which comes from third sources that people were wearing civilian clothes. Whether it is complete or not, the witness couldn't tell us. He doesn't draw any conclusions apart from that, in general terms, clothing may be an element in identifying a victim, as a child, as a woman, as -- even perhaps as a civilian. But are there any conclusions on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm confused, Your Honour. On page -- I'm at page 77 of the hard copy right now, and I believe it has a very specific conclusion that says, This would have enabled the shooter to identify her as a civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would enable. Of course, not she was a civilian, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So as he has explained in other parts of the report, clothing may assist. And "would have enabled," is, of course, is a very soft language, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if it's in an expert report that's being presented for criminal liability, I don't think anything is very soft, Your Honour, to be honest with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, perhaps there's a difference of interpretation of what the report says here, that it was an element which would lead rather in the direction of the person being a civilian than a military person. That seems to be the issue. The point you wanted to make seems to be clear to me. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that for all three of these Unscheduled Incidents that we have in this section of your report the source of fire given to you by the Prosecution was exclusively VRS positions, Army of Republika Srpska positions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree. I was given the location only, so I know that the Sharpstone was the point of origin. At that time of the report, I wasn't provided with a map that showed the positions, so I only point where the -- where I think the shooter must have been, and if that coincides with VRS positions, then he might have been VRS. I don't anywhere indicate that the shooter was VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me see if I can understand your methodology. You obtained from the Prosecution's investigator a set of coordinates for a probable sniper location, or shooter location; let's keep it simple. You go into the field, you do your analysis, and you either verify that that position is possible, or you exclude that position as being a possibility. In the event that you verify a possibility for that location to be the source of fire, do you stop looking for other potential sources of fire that could also be potentially possible sources for the fire. That is, also have an equal line of sight to the target, that also are within ranges that weapons and ammunition could reach? That's what I'm asking, sir.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I take into account all possibilities and then eliminate them on technical possibility, and after technical, I will go to tactical possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say you eliminate -- that you take into account all possibilities and then eliminate them, how could you take into account the BiH positions and either eliminate them or verify them, if you were not given those positions by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, the reports -- I visited the village of Sedrenik and Sharpstone twice. The first time I wasn't able to visit Sharpstone itself, since it was -- there was still mine clearing going on at the location, and there was a heavy fog. I did see trenches at the -- around Sharpstone, so that it's a indication there were at least positions from either party. And for the BiH positions, I was given a general line where the -- of where the BiH positions had been which was at the -- at the base of Sharpstone, and unless the BiH positions would have been in houses immediately bordering on the square where the incident took place, then it could have been from those positions. But from what I understood, the information provided to me, was that the -- that the BiH didn't have any positions on that -- on that intersection where the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that for each of these Unscheduled Incidents, your conclusions presuppose that the victims were the intended targets of the shooter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you further agree with me that for each of those three Unscheduled Incidents, your conclusions presuppose that the shooter was a trained sniper, rather than a marksman or ordinary soldier?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you further agree with me that for each of these three Unscheduled Incidents, your exclusions presuppose that the shooter used a weapon equipped with an optical sight capable of magnification of at least four times?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Presuppose, I don't know if that's the correct word for it. I do believe that if the shooter wouldn't have a optical sight, he would have great difficulty in even spotting the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to the second of the Unscheduled Incidents. Page 73 in the hard copy, page 74 of the e-court in English, and I have page 94 in B/C/S, if that is accurate. And, for this incident, we see here that you have listed the alleged shooting position being 850 to 950 metres away from the target? Based upon our earlier discussion, would you agree that this would be what you had termed a very difficult long shot -- long-range shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's a difficult long-range shot, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you cannot know if there are any other targets in the area on that day that may have been the intended target which resulted in a missed shot that could have struck this victim in the manner we discussed before?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn to page 78 in the hard copy, 79 in the English in e-court, page 100 in the B/C/S in e-court, we should be looking at the third Unscheduled Incident. And I'd like to ask you with respect to that incident -- I guess it's actually page -- yeah. 79 in e-court, 78 in hard copy. The alleged shooting position was 950 to 1.050 metres from the victim. Would this also qualify as a long-range shot scenario?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in this case, would you agree with me that you cannot know if there were any other targets in the area on the day of the incident that may have been the intended target which resulted in a missed shot that could have struck this victim in the manner we discussed before?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here, on this page, it is recorded that the victim heard 20 or more shots. Now, you attribute this to being a machine-gun that was firing at her. I put it to you, sir, that you have missed a very plausible and common-sense explanation that there was an exchange of gun-fire between combatant forces and that the 20 shots didn't have to come from the same weapon. Would you agree with me that you cannot exclude to a degree of scientific certainty that this, in fact, was the case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Could you rephrase that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Would you agree with me that another plausible possibility for this woman hearing 20 shots is that there was an active exchange of gun-fire between combatant forces and that the 20 shots did not come from the same weapon?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I agree that if someone hears 20 shots there is a possibility. However, with the positions on top of Sharpstone and positions on the lower slopes of Sharpstone, the difference in sound would have been a lot different -- would have been very different than if she -- if the victim would have positions very close by. I don't believe that as in the other incidents that it's a possibility that there was a missed shell because of the geographical situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you a different question, sir. You have gone on record in your report basing the fact that the weapon that must have been used in this incident was a machine-gun, and you based that on the fact that the victim states hearing 20 or more shots just after she was hit. My question for you, sir, is how did you exclude the possibility that the 20 or more shots she heard was return fire or some other type of fire as opposed to being from the same weapon? What scientific method did you use to exclude that possibility?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would, Your Honour, just object to the form of the question that he has gone on record as saying that it must be this. Because that is not exactly what he says in his report. Where it says "it indicates."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about Unscheduled 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Page 78 in the hard copy. And it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the two machine-guns left is the weapon that must have been used in this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Hochhauser, seems to be rather strong conclusion. Nothing but one of the two machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I missed that sentence. I was looking at the first sentence of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you to please answer my question. As an expert trained in your field, what scientific method did you utilise to exclude the possibility that the 20 or more shots she heard were from other weapons.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: What scientific method is something that I would not really call it, but it's -- it's based on the sound and distance, so the time -- the time-lapse between them is she heard 20 or more shots. If there were weapons that had been fired at the same time at other targets in her area, she would experience those 20 shots possibly from more weapons. That's a -- that's true. But if there had been an exchange of fire at that distance because the -- the fighting line was -- the front line was approximately 750 metres away from her position, she would hardly be able to hear shooting that was going on at short range with other calibre weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm looking at the clock. We have to conclude for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us an estimate as to how much time you would still need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe I'll still on track to finish within the, I believe, three and a half hours that we had anticipated for this witness. I believe we have used up an hour and a half today, so that would mean two hours tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two hours -- two sessions tomorrow. Mr. Van der Weijden, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any other way, with whomever, about your testimony, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom, I. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Friday, the 11th of January, at 9.30 in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of January, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.
